title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
layout_note: One left-to-right row: frame stack -> image encoder -> memory attention -> mask decoder (with prompt encoder beneath) -> predicted frame -> memory encoder -> memory bank; several feedback arrows leave the memory bank, run back along the top and drop into memory attention. Every block is drawn with faded copies behind it to suggest earlier frames.
grouping: No frames or containers: each module is one pastel shape with faded translucent copies stacked behind it (offset up-left) to show the time dimension; colour alone separates modules.
shapes_depth: Flat pastel shapes with no outlines: encoders as trapezoids (green image encoder narrowing right, pink memory encoder), memory attention, mask decoder, prompt encoder and memory bank as rounded rectangles in light blue, peach, lavender and pink, with bold dark serif labels. Inputs and outputs are real video frames, the output frame with a green mask over the object. Feedback arrows are thin grey lines with right-angle bends, the nearest one darker and older ones paler.
proposed_highlight: The streaming-memory parts (memory attention, memory encoder, memory bank) are new modules in the row, and the memory loop is the only path drawn over the top of the pipeline; there is no extra colour or frame marking them.
lesson: Draw a streaming, frame-by-frame model by stacking faded translucent copies behind each module and the input frame, and run the memory feedback as nested right-angle return lines over the top that fade with age.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2408.00714); the first page shows no venue (v2, Meta FAIR); remembered venue ICLR 2025 (not verified in this session). The automatic crop failed because SAM 2's captions have no colon or period after the figure number; the figure was cropped by hand from page 5 with PyMuPDF (bbox 68.9,46.8,543.1,169.4 pt) and its embedded photos recorded in fig3.json.

arrangement.units: one unframed row of modules; time shown by faded copies behind each module rather than by panels
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real video frames with a diagonal 'time' arrow at the left edge; prompts as the words mask, points, box under the prompt encoder
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the predicted mask is a real frame with a coloured overlay in the middle of the row
arrangement.shared: the memory bank's output is drawn as several return arrows over the top, one per stored frame, all landing on the single memory attention block

core.what: a left-to-right per-frame chain (frame -> image encoder -> memory attention -> mask decoder -> masked frame -> memory encoder -> memory bank) closed by grey lines that run back over the top from the memory bank into memory attention, with past frames as faded stacked copies behind every element

relations.form: one horizontal row of modules joined by short dark arrows, the input photo at the left and the masked photo in the middle

every element has two or three faded copies stacked behind it along a 'time' diagonal, and four lines of decreasing darkness loop from the memory bank stack over the top into the memory attention stack
the memory bank sits at the right end of the row and its stored memories return to memory attention on the overhead lines
a lavender prompt encoder directly below the mask decoder takes mask, points and box as text labels and feeds up into the decoder with three short arrows

channels.colour: fill = module identity (green image encoder, blue memory attention, orange mask decoder, lavender prompt encoder); pink marks both memory encoder and memory bank, grouping the memory path; the mask is a green tint on the photo
channels.shape: trapezoids = encoders, rounded rectangles = other modules, photos = frames
channels.line: opacity = time: the darkest return line and front copy are the current frame, fainter lines and copies are older frames

quality.strengths: the streaming memory is drawn as geometry: stacked faded copies give the time axis and the overhead lines give the recurrence without a separate diagram; opacity carries one meaning (age) for both copies and lines; the main row is straight with short arrows
quality.weaknesses: the memories themselves are not drawn as data - the bank is a box and its contents are only faded copies of that box; the prompts are text labels; the predicted mask is a small green tint on the photo, easy to miss

insights.structure: All seven parts sit on one horizontal row, with the prompt encoder dropped just below the mask decoder and a memory loop arching back over the top from the memory bank to memory attention.
insights.data: Input and output are real video frames, each a stack of fading copies receding up-left, and the output frame carries a green mask overlay; prompts are the plain words mask, points and box with up-arrows.
insights.emphasis: Recurrence is the visual idea: every module has ghosted copies behind it and the memory feedback lines fade from dark (latest) to pale (oldest), so the memory mechanism stands out without a highlight colour.
insights.flow: Short dark arrows run left to right along the row; the grey return lines leave the memory bank upward, run left along the top with right-angle bends and drop into memory attention.
insights.avoid: The ghosted copies are very faint and the return lines stack close together, which makes it hard to count how many memories feed back.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
